patient.name: Derek Munoz
patient.chiefComplaint: Combative, agitated behavior, suspected stimulant use

history.hpi: Police were called to a convenience store parking lot for a shirtless man yelling incoherently and pounding on parked cars. Officers restrained him with soft cuffs prior to EMS arrival. He remains combative, shouting, and profusely diaphoretic with dilated pupils. An empty small plastic baggie was found near him.
history.events: Police restrained the patient after he was found shirtless, yelling, and striking parked vehicles; EMS called to scene by responding officers

scene.dispatch: 32-year-old male, combative, police on scene, parking lot
scene.location: Parking lot outside a convenience store, well-lit, police perimeter established around the patient
scene.safety: Scene secured by law enforcement prior to EMS entry; patient in soft restraints applied by police; potential for continued violence, officers remaining on scene
scene.bystanders: Store clerk reports the patient was yelling incoherently and tore off his shirt before police arrived; no witnesses confirm drug use
visualCues: Empty small plastic baggie found near patient by police

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 32-year-old male in police soft restraints, shouting, thrashing, and diaphoretic with dilated pupils. Vitals show marked tachycardia, hypertension, tachypnea, and hyperthermia consistent with stimulant toxicity and severe agitation.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, bounding, skin hot and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Thrashing against restraints, superhuman-seeming strength, unable to formally assess strength/sensation
otherFindings: No visible trauma noted on brief exam
Skin hot to touch, concerning for hyperthermia
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Get off me! You're not real, get away from me!"

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes a high violence risk, uses a validated risk assessment tool, and administers the ketamine sedation dose (4 mg/kg IM) per the Agitated/Violent Patient protocol.

phases.name: Sedation dose ketamine given
phases.description: Crew attempts brief verbal de-escalation, risk-stratifies the patient as high violence risk, ensures police restraints do not restrict chest wall movement, and administers ketamine 4 mg/kg IM for chemical restraint. A cardiac monitor and capnography are applied, and external cooling is started for suspected hyperthermia.
phases.triggerCondition: After a brief attempt at verbal reassurance fails given the severity of agitation, the crew risk-stratifies the patient as high violence risk and proceeds with ketamine sedation dosing, monitoring, and cooling per the Agitated/Violent Patient and Stimulant Poisoning/Overdose protocols.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin warm and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Cooling measures started (ice packs to axilla/groin)

expectedActions.shortAction: Attempt brief verbal reassurance/de-escalation before pharmacologic or physical management
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt verbal reassurance and calm patient prior to use of pharmacologic and/or physical management devices
expectedActions.rationale: De-escalation is the first-line step even when severity ultimately requires chemical restraint.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Use a validated risk tool (RASS/AMSS/BARS) to risk-stratify the patient as high violence risk
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use a validated risk assessment tool such as RASS (Richmond Agitation Sedation Score), AMSS (Altered Mental Status Score), or BARS (Behavioral Activity Rating Scale) to risk stratify violent patients to help guide interventions
expectedActions.rationale: Risk stratification guides selection of the sedation-level ketamine dose over lower-tier alternatives.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Secure all four extremities to the stationary stretcher frame without restricting chest wall motion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Secure all four extremities to maximize safety for patient, staff, and others Secure all extremities to the stationary frame of the stretcher
expectedActions.rationale: Proper restraint technique protects against positional asphyxia while maintaining scene safety.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Ketamine 340 mg IM (85 kg × 4 mg/kg) for chemical restraint of high-violence-risk agitation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ketamine (option for high violence risk) — Adults: 4 mg/kg IM; 3–5 minute onset of action
expectedActions.rationale: The sedation-tier ketamine dose is substantially higher than the analgesic dose and is what achieves effective chemical restraint.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply cardiac monitor and capnography; watch closely for hypoventilation/oversedation after ketamine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Apply a cardiac monitor as soon as possible, particularly when pharmacologic management medications have been administered All patients who have received pharmacologic management medications must be monitored closely for the development of hypoventilation and oversedation Utilize capnography if available
expectedActions.rationale: Ketamine sedation carries a risk of respiratory depression that must be caught early.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Begin external cooling with cold/ice packs to axilla and groin for suspected hyperthermia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If hyperthermia suspected, begin external cooling (e.g., cold or ice packs to axilla/groin)
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperthermia from prolonged agitation and stimulant toxicity is a major driver of morbidity/mortality.

transitions.condition: Adequate ketamine sedation controls the agitation; cardiac monitor, capnography, and external cooling are maintained while the patient is packaged and transported.

Crew mistakenly administers the lower analgesic ketamine dose (0.25 mg/kg IM, per the Pain Management protocol) instead of the 4 mg/kg IM sedation dose, leaving the patient inadequately sedated and still combative.

phases.name: Cooling and monitoring maintained
phases.description: The patient is adequately sedated, no longer combative, and cooling has begun reducing his temperature. Crew maintains continuous respiratory and cardiac monitoring en route given the risk of delayed hypoventilation after ketamine sedation.
phases.triggerCondition: After the sedation-dose ketamine takes effect and cooling and monitoring are maintained, the patient calms, allowing safe packaging and transport with continued close observation.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin cooling, less diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: No longer thrashing, minimal spontaneous movement
otherFindings: Restraints remain in place per protocol until fully cooperative

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously monitor airway patency, respiratory status, SpO2/EtCO2, and cardiac status en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Continuous monitoring of: Airway patency Respiratory status with pulse oximetry and/or capnography Circulatory status with frequent blood pressure measurements Mental status and trends in level of patient cooperation Cardiac status, especially if the patient has received pharmacologic management medication
expectedActions.rationale: Sedated patients require ongoing vigilance for delayed respiratory depression.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess and document mental status trend and circulatory status serially en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Repeated assessment of mental status and trends in the level of patient cooperation Repeated assessment of circulatory status with blood pressure, capillary refill, cardiac monitoring
expectedActions.rationale: Serial documentation tracks response to sedation and cooling and supports handoff.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency

phases.name: Sub-therapeutic ketamine dose given
phases.description: Ketamine was dosed at the lower analgesic range (0.25 mg/kg IM) rather than the sedation range (4 mg/kg IM). The patient remains combative and hyperthermic, continuing to struggle against restraints with ongoing risk for delirium-associated cardiac arrest and positional asphyxia.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew confuses the Pain Management protocol's analgesic ketamine dose (0.25 mg/kg IM) with the Agitated/Violent Patient protocol's sedation dose (4 mg/kg IM); the sub-therapeutic dose fails to control the agitation.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, bounding, skin hot and diaphoretic
otherFindings: No reduction in agitation after initial dose
Increasing risk of positional asphyxia from prolonged struggle against restraints
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Get away! Get away from me!" (still yelling, disorganized)

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize 21 mg IM (85 kg × 0.25 mg/kg) is an analgesic dose only, inadequate for chemical restraint of this agitation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ketamine: 0.25 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose 25 mg; maximum cumulative dose 100 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Confusing the analgesic dosing range with the sedation/chemical-restraint range leaves the patient dangerously under-sedated and at risk for positional asphyxia.

expectedActions.shortAction: Redose ketamine to reach 340 mg IM total (85 kg × 4 mg/kg sedation dose) for adequate chemical restraint
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ketamine (option for high violence risk) — Adults: 4 mg/kg IM; 3–5 minute onset of action
expectedActions.rationale: Correcting to the sedation-tier dose is necessary to control agitation and prevent cardiopulmonary decompensation from prolonged struggle.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Agitated or Violent Patient/Behavioral Emergency
